summary: In this excerpt from the fiction 'Book 3 — part 194', a woman calls Steve, who is at his hotel in Belize City, to share news she heard from the pharmacist at the corner. They are apart and talk over a satellite connection while she takes a test that turns bright pink. Steve is speechless, and the two then argue playfully about naming the child Max, his father's middle name, and what to call a girl.
one_line: A woman and her partner, separated by distance, share a pink-test moment by phone and banter over baby names.
key_facts: The clock above the sink read eight-thirty when the narrator called Steve.
Steve was back at his hotel in Belize City.
The narrator got Steve on the first try.
The narrator had been feeling strange, and some things had been a little behind schedule.
The narrator said she had just heard something from the pharmacist at the corner.
The narrator and Steve could not be together, so they shared the moment over a satellite connection.
The narrator was doing the test right then, using a stick taken out of a glass holder.
When the narrator pulled out the stick, it was a bright, beautiful pink.
Steve was speechless for a long moment and finally said, 'Wow.'
The narrator said, 'This, I realized, is the most incredible moment in any woman's life.'
Steve's voice went up an octave when he said 'Max.'
Max is the name of Steve's dad's middle name, and Steve wants to name the baby Max as an old family tradition.
The narrator warned Steve not to say Maxine, or she would divorce him before making an honest woman of her.
Steve said that if the baby is a girl, the narrator gets to pick the name.
